newsitem.title: SPAIN: BCH soars pre-Q1 results, favourable chart.
newsitem.headline: BCH soars pre-Q1 results, favourable chart.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Banco Central Hispano jumped 2.74 percent on Monday, outpacing the overall market and the sector given expectations for strong earnings in the first-quarter and a favourable technical outlook.
"The perspectives for results are good and that is encouraging people to take positions," a dealer said.
At 1215 GMT, the share had risen 110 pesetas, or 2.74 percent to 4,130. The IBEX index of 35 leading shares was up just 27.01 points, or 0.48 percent to 5,655.16.

Analysts polled by Reuters expect on average a rise of 20.2 percent in first-quarter net attributable earnings, which the bank is to report on Thursday. One dealer said some in the market were looking for a rise of up to 25 percent.
"The share had lagged behind others and its results are going to be good," a trader at a Spanish bank said.
Juan Berberana, analyst at AB Asesores, said "People are buying ahead of the results...There is domestic interest in the share - people are playing the recuperation story."
Other banks were also faring well, although not as strongly as BCH. Bankinter was up 1.62 percent, while Santander was up 1.30 percent.
The technical outlook was also helping the bank, dealers said, after the share broke through a resistance band below 4,000 last week.

"Last week, BCH was facing key resistance which it broke at the end of the week in heavy volume. Today, the break was confirmed and it doesn't have short-term resistance," an analyst at a brokerage said.
Last week, the share broke through peaks of 3,904 and of 3,940, set on February 17 and March 10, respectively. But one dealer said it still needed to breach 4,160 to clear its path.
BCH's decision, announced on Friday, to end talks with Banco de Colombia on a strategic partnership was also helping the share, dealers said.
"The news on Friday is very good for the share. If it breaks 4,160, it could go up more," the dealer said.
BCH's expected expression of interest in bidding for Spain's second telephone operator Retevision had little impact, as any effects would only be felt very long term on the share.
"Retevision won't have a short-term effect," Berberana said.
